description:
FILED s534a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from the method-lookup probe matrix (scratch/s534a/pr/matrix.pl row 45).  PRE-EXISTING on main 95a1de03 (code sha).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3):

    package Q::Base; sub m { "Q::Base::m" }
    package main;
    my @r = do { package Q::Kid4; use parent -norequire, "Q::Base"; 7 }; print "3 @r\n";

perl: `3 7`.  PCL: the run dies `The function common-lisp:nil is undefined.` (a raw SBCL error, untrappable shape).  The same with `eval { package X; use parent ...; ... }` and with `use base`.  A BARE block `{ package X; use parent ...; }` is right.

MECHANISM (read from `./pl2cl` output): the do-block lowers to `(funcall (lambda () ...))`, and the `use parent` statement's preamble forms -- `(p-eval-always (p-defpackage :|Q::Base|))` and `(p-defclass |Q::Kid4|::plc-q-kid4 ("Q::Base") ())` -- are spliced in BETWEEN `funcall` and the lambda:

    (funcall
      (p-eval-always (p-defpackage :|Q::Base|))
      (p-defclass |Q::Kid4|::plc-q-kid4 ("Q::Base") ())
      (lambda () ...))

so `funcall` calls the value of `p-eval-always` (NIL).  Layer: Pl/Parser2.pm, where a statement's hoisted preamble forms are attached to the enclosing expression-block lowering (the do/eval BLOCK value form); they belong before the funcall (or inside the lambda body's head), as the bare-block path places them.

Probes: scratch/s534a/pr/p45.pl (four spellings), p45b.pl (the minimal one) in the s534a worktree.  BAR: the reproducer prints `3 7`; the four p45.pl spellings print perl's output; a guard row in an existing Pl/t file.
subject: PCL compiler: `use parent` / `use base` inside a do BLOCK or eval BLOCK that switches package dies "The function common-lisp:nil is undefined" -- the use's preamble forms are emitted as ARGUMENTS of the block's funcall
